paper_metadata.title: The Lie Algebra of XY-mixer Topologies and Warm Starting QAOA for Constrained Optimization

summary: The paper studies warm-started multi-angle QAOA for constrained optimization using an XY-mixer on three problems: portfolio optimization, graph partitioning, and sparsest k-subgraph. It reports simulated improvements in approximation ratio and success probability on instances with n = 12, 14, 16 assets/vertices and circuit depths up to p = 40 for portfolio optimization and p = 24 for the graph problems, but no hardware execution or demonstrated quantum advantage over classical methods.

experiments.description: Warm-started multi-angle QAOA for portfolio optimization on SP500 instances, comparing random initialization vs warm start across multiple circuit depths and asset counts.

algorithm.ansatz: XY-mixer QAOA with RZ phase separators; full ansatz adds RZZ terms
algorithm.convergence_criteria: 100 training steps for restricted circuit, then 100 training steps for full circuit

hyperparameters.phase_separators: RZ only for warm start; RZ + RZZ for full circuit

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Random uniform in [0, 2π] for restricted circuit; transfer learned RZ and XY parameters to full circuit and initialize RZZ angles to 0

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 binary variable per asset; select exactly k=n/2 assets
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x -p^T x + q x^T C x subject to |x| = k
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: XY-mixer preserves Hamming weight; Dicke-state initialization; no penalty terms in the gate-based warm-start circuit
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_f = H_p + q H_covar, with H_p = -∑_i p_i σ_i^1 and H_covar = ∑_{i,j} C_{ij} σ_i^1 σ_j^1

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization on monthly SP500 data

dataset_specification.description: Top-performing stocks selected from publicly available SP500 trading data between 2010 and 2018; k=n/2 assets chosen

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Daily returns computed from price series; monthly average returns and covariance matrices constructed from 84 months of data; top n stocks selected by average return per month
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Median performance over the best of 10 randomly initialized QAOA-p circuits across 84 instances; compared random start vs warm start; metrics: approximation ratio and log success probability

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct expected returns and covariance matrices from SP500 data; select top n stocks per month
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute approximation ratio and success probability from final state

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: warm start begins with better approximation ratio and improves smoothly; random start worse

speedup_claims.caveats: No classical algorithmic baseline or speedup claim is reported; the paper compares random initialization vs warm start within QAOA.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Warm-start restricted circuit uses polynomial-sized DLA; full circuit has exponential-sized DLA
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: NP-hard for arbitrary p, C; polynomial if k=O(1)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No hardware execution; numerical simulation in PennyLane only. Restricted warm-start circuit uses 2np parameters; full circuit uses (n^2+3n)p/2 parameters.
limiting_factors: No classical baseline beyond random initialization
Warm-start improvement is within a simulated QAOA workflow, not a demonstrated quantum advantage

notes: Hardware is not tied to a named QPU; PennyLane is explicitly reported, and the work is presented as numerical experiments/simulation rather than hardware execution.
num_qubits inferred from the reported asset counts and the circuit definition using n qubits for n assets.
The paper reports improved approximation ratio and success probability from warm starting, but only within simulation and without a classical algorithmic baseline that would establish advantage.
